edges.description: Loss of the sorting motif stops pro-EGF from reaching the basolateral membrane of polarized epithelial cells; apical delivery is unaffected.
Without basolateral EGF, the basolateral EGF receptor of DCT cells is under-stimulated.
EGFR stimulation activates TRPM6 through Src-family kinases and Rac1, which move TRPM6 from intracellular stores to the plasma membrane, and through ERK/AP-1, which raises TRPM6 transcription.
Reduced TRPM6-mediated reabsorption lets magnesium escape in the urine.
The tubular defect is measured clinically as renal magnesium wasting.
Continuing urinary loss lowers serum magnesium.
Mutant pro-EGF fails to deliver TRPM6-stimulating activity to the basolateral medium.
edges.limitations: MDCK is a canine kidney line, and TRPM6 activity is read out in a separate HEK293 overexpression system rather than in DCT cells.

nodes.description: Urinary magnesium stays relatively high despite low serum magnesium, which shows a tubular reabsorption defect. Magnesium infusion studies showed a lowered renal threshold with a normal tubular maximum. Urinary calcium is normal, which separates this disorder from the hypercalciuric forms of renal magnesium wasting.
